references.text: The Israelites had just left Elim, where there were twelve springs and seventy palm trees, before they came to the Desert of Sin.
Numbers gives a parallel travel route confirming that the Israelites left Elim and camped at the Sea of Reeds, then in the Desert of Sin.
The reference to the second month after leaving Egypt relates to the time of Passover and the Exodus month, which was established as the first month.
The Israelites continued from the Desert of Sin and arrived at the Desert of Sinai in the third month, showing the geographical and chronological progression of the wilderness journey.
Ezekiel refers to the wilderness journey and how God brought Israel out of Egypt and led them through the desert.
Stephen's speech in Acts mentions Moses leading the Israelites out of Egypt and through the wilderness for forty years.
The Letter to the Hebrews refers to the Israelites' wilderness journey and warns against hardening hearts as their ancestors did in the desert.
Direct narrative continuation: 16:1 arrives at Sin, while 17:1 leaves it.
Chronological confirmation of the arrival at the Desert of Sin, but with a textual discrepancy regarding the starting point (Elim vs. the Sea of Reeds).
Theological contrast: First arrival (God's provision) versus last arrival (Miriam's death) at the same place.
